domain: Illegal occupation. Contains the single most damaging error in circulation on this subject.

rules.statement: Allanamiento de morada, art. 202.1 CP, six months to two years prison, applies where the property is a morada. Usurpacion with violence, art. 245.1, one to two years. Peaceful occupation of a property that is not a morada, art. 245.2, a fine of three to six months.

source.name: BOE consolidated text
source.ref: Instruccion 1/2020 Fiscalia General del Estado, quoting the Codigo Penal

rules.statement: Second residences and seasonal residences ARE a morada, provided the legitimate occupiers carry on their private life there, even occasionally.
rules.notes: THE MOST USEFUL FACT FOR OUR AUDIENCE, and it cuts in their favour. A holiday home in regular personal use can be a morada, which makes the occupation the more serious art. 202 offence and opens the door to precautionary eviction. A purely investment property, empty and never personally used, likely falls under art. 245.2, a fine-level offence. A tool should give the test and say it turns on evidence of personal use. It must not tell a customer which one applies.

rules.statement: There is no 48-hour rule in Spanish law. It does not exist as legislation and it is not Spanish police operational practice.
rules.notes: THE ORIGIN OF THE MYTH IS VISIBLE IN THE SOURCE ITSELF. Instruccion 1/2020 mentions 48 hours only as a FOREIGN comparison, describing French police powers, alongside a 24-hour reference for Germany. Spain has no equivalent. What exists instead is a test, not a clock: solid indications the offence was committed, urgency and harm to the legitimate possessor, and proportionality. CORRECT FRAMING: speed matters because it supports flagrancia and the urgency test, not because any statute grants a 48-hour window. The 48-hour rule is stated as Spanish law across most English-language guidance on this subject. It is not.

rules.statement: Ley Organica 1/2025 added allanamiento de morada and usurpacion to the fast-track criminal route in art. 795.1.2 LECrim, with effect from 3 April 2025. The trial is listed within fifteen days of the guard court stage.

source.name: BOE consolidated text
source.ref: Circular 1/2025 Fiscalia General del Estado, 26 June 2025

rules.notes: PARTIAL: disposicion final 38 of LO 1/2025 lists exceptions to the 3 April date and could not be read, so confirm the LECrim amendment is not among them. This is a criminal trial listed within fifteen days, NOT a fifteen-day eviction. Timelines of 18 months to 2 years predate this reform.

rules.statement: The civil express recovery route under art. 250.1.4 LEC is open to natural persons, non-profits with a right to possess, and public social-housing bodies. Occupiers have five days to justify a title.

source.name: BOE consolidated text
source.ref: Ley 5/2018 de 11 de junio, arts. 250.1.4 and 441.1 bis LEC

rules.notes: LOAD-BEARING FOR OUR AUDIENCE: an owner who holds the property through a company or SL is EXCLUDED from this route and must use the ordinary one. No 2025 or 2026 amendment extending it to legal persons was found.
